author: JILL ZIMA BORSKI
title: District eyes 21.5% higher tax hike - NewsBreak
text:
By JILL ZIMA BORSKI ,
7 hours ago
KEY LARGO — The Key Largo Fire and EMS District on Monday, Sept. 8, proposed a millage rate for fiscal year 2025-2026 of 1.3371, which is 21.51% over the rollback rate, or the tax rate that would generate the same amount of revenue as this fiscal year.
The fiscal year runs from Oct. 1, 2025 to Sept. 30, 2026.
The district board’s budget hearing was at the fire station at mile marker 99, oceanside.
The district’s boundaries extend to the junction of County Road 905 and 905A and include up to Morris Lane/Manatee Bay Marina on U.S.1 near mile marker 112.5. The boundaries encompass the islands of Key Largo and Cross Key.
This year’s millage rate was 1.1975, or $119.75 in taxes for everyone $100,000 of taxable property value. The proposed rate of 1.3371, or $133.71 per $100,000, would generate more than 21% more tax revenue due to rising property values.
With the current taxable property value of $6.499 billion in the district, to raise the same amount of money of this year, the millage would equate to 1.1004, or $110.04 per $100.000 of value.
However, demands for higher salaries and related benefits by the district's fire-rescue and EMS service providers led to the request being a fifth higher than a year ago. The budget total currently is set at $14.8 million for 2025-2026, but could be lowered at the final hearing set for 6 p.m. Monday, Sept. 22.
The district currently has an unassigned fund balance (or reserves) of $4.434 million. The district also sets aside funds for vehicle replacement and has $1.636 million allocated in that fund. A 2016 ambulance is set to be replaced in the coming year and has an estimated replacement cost of $631,430.
The district board’s yearly expenses, which includes the board of five commissioners, clerk and services like accounting and advertising, are estimated at about $349,000, which is about $46,000 higher than this year’s budget.
Because of fire-rescue and EMS staff’s overtime pay equating to $206,254 this fiscal year, the district is proposing new positions for a total of 27 employees for 2025-2026. This would lead to an increase in salaries and wages of $769,395. Stipends for captains and divisional lead officers also are expected to increase by $18,000 over the current year.
The district’s medical director yearly compensation is expected to increase to $67,000.
After a lengthy discussion, district board Chair Tony Allen asked the fire-rescue and EMS departments to bring back lower budget proposals to the final budget hearing.
